title: Ampleness near a schematic fibre over a Noetherian base
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning a scheme with a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $f:X\to T$ be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $L$ be a line module on $X$. Here proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every base change. A line module on an algebraic space is an $\mathcal O$-module on its small etale site locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a morphism $a:Z\to W$, write $a^*M=\mathcal O_Z\otimes_{a^{-1}\mathcal O_W}a^{-1}M$ using its canonical ringed etale topoi [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]; on schemes use the corresponding ordinary invertible module [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence, def-sc-invertible-module]. For a line module $N$ on a space $Z$ over a scheme $B$, relatively ample means that $Z$ is a scheme and $N$ is ample on the inverse image of every affine open of $B$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Let $t\in T$, put $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, and suppose $X_t$ is a scheme and $L_t$ is ample. There is an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq T$ of $t$ such that $X_V$ is a scheme and $L_V$ is relatively ample over $V$.

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood); relative ampleness is Definition 0D31 and its scheme-base sanity check 0D32.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model] for the tensor pullbacks. Pulling back a trivialization of a line and its inverse shows that its pullback and its tensor powers remain lines; multiplying elementary tensors identifies pullback of a tensor power with the power of the pullback. On schemes [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies these lines, their sections and their pullbacks with the ordinary invertible modules. If $X_t$ is empty, properness makes $f(|X|)$ closed, and $t$ is outside it. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ in its complement by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Then $X_V$ is the empty scheme, and ampleness on every affine inverse image is vacuous by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Hence assume $X_t$ nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), preliminary line-module interpretation and empty-fibre case

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-ample-fibre-section-lifting] to obtain a bound $a$. The scheme $X_t$ is proper over $\kappa(t)$ by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change], hence locally of finite type. Apply [lem-trf-affine-eventual-power-immersion] to its ample line $L_t$. Choose $d\geq\max(a,1)$ large enough to obtain an immersion $j:X_t\to\mathbf P^r_{\kappa(t)}$ and $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L_t^{\otimes d}$. Projective space is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Thus $j$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] and a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed]. The canonical isomorphism $\theta$ of [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] between this relative-Proj projective space and $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};\kappa(t))$ lies over the base and is, on the affine chart, the Proj comparison fixing every $T_i$; it therefore matches the standard opens $D_+(T_i)$, the coordinates $T_l/T_i$ and the twists glued from them, so the base-change-model statements below apply. Pull back the standard coordinates using $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L_t^{\otimes d}$ to get sections $v_0,\ldots,v_r$ generating $L_t^{\otimes d}$: each coordinate trivializes on its chart and these charts cover, by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. Their associated morphism is $j$ by the quotient classification in [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry].

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), first paragraph, choice of a sufficiently high projective embedding on the fibre

proof.text: For each of the finitely many $v_i$, apply [lem-sfb-space-ample-fibre-section-lifting] at this same $d$. Intersect their neighbourhoods and choose an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $t$ inside the intersection by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Restrict all lifts to get $s_i\in\Gamma(X_U,L^{\otimes d})$ with fibre tuple $(v_i)$. Replace $T$ by $U$ and $X$ by $X_U$. Properness persists by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. The Noetherian hypothesis was used before this replacement; no new application of the lifting lemma is needed.

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), first paragraph, simultaneous lifting of the finitely many coordinates

proof.text: Put $M=L^{\otimes d}$. The locus $G$ where the $s_i$ generate $M$ is open: on a scheme etale chart trivializing $M$, write $s_i=a_i e$; its inverse image is $\bigcup_iD(a_i)$. These opens agree under change of trivialization and pullback; [lem-trf-etale-open-chart-morphism-descent] gives the corresponding open subspace of $X$. The fibre lies in $G$ since the $v_i$ generate. The complement $C=|X|\setminus|G|$ is closed, so $f(C)$ is closed and misses $t$. Replace $T$ by an affine neighbourhood of $t$ inside $T\setminus f(C)$ and restrict $X$. Now the $s_i$ generate $M$ everywhere. Properness is preserved by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), first paragraph, deleting the proper image of the nongeneration locus

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $p:A\to X$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. On $A$, [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] applied to the quotient $\mathcal O_A^{r+1}\twoheadrightarrow p^*M$ constructs a $T$-map $A\to P=\mathbf P^r_T$ and a quotient-compatible twist isomorphism. Naturality of that statement makes the two maps equal on the scheme $A\times_XA$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-open-chart-morphism-descent] with the whole atlas as its invariant open to descend a unique $\varphi:X\to P$. The local twist isomorphisms also agree on $A\times_XA$: each sends the same pulled-back coordinate sections to the $s_i$, and those sections generate. They therefore give an isomorphism $\varphi^*\mathcal O_P(1)\cong M$ of module sheaves on the small etale site. Explicitly a local section is sent by the local maps after pulling back to the atlas, and their equality on overlaps gives its unique glued image; the inverses glue in the same way. The same construction on any scheme test gives the quotient morphism there, by the atlas descent's test-scheme clause. In particular the fibre map is $j$, and, once $X$ is a scheme, the descended map is its ordinary quotient morphism. This supplies the projective-space construction whose details the source omits.

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), first paragraph, omitted algebraic-space construction of phi and its hyperplane pullback

proof.text: The map $q:P\to T$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], transported along the isomorphism $\theta:P\cong\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};T)$ over $T$ of [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space]; hence $q$ is separated. The graph $\Gamma_\varphi:X\to X\times_TP$ is the pullback of $\Delta_q:P\to P\times_TP$ by $(\varphi\operatorname{pr}_X,\operatorname{pr}_P)$. It is therefore a closed immersion on every scheme test: [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] applies to that test and $\Delta_q$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper] the graph is proper. The projection $X\times_TP\to P$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. Their composite $\varphi$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition].

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), last paragraph, properness of phi via its closed graph

proof.text: Let $Q\subseteq|X|$ be the quasi-finite locus of $\varphi$; it is open by [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open]. For every point $z\in|P_t|$, the fibre of $\varphi$ over $z$ is the base change of the closed immersion $j$ to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$, hence is a closed subscheme of that field spectrum by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. It is empty or that one-point scheme, because a field has only the zero and unit ideals. By [lem-sfb-space-finite-fibre-quasifinite-criterion], all points of $X$ over $z$ lie in $Q$. Thus the closed set $\varphi(|X|\setminus Q)$ misses the entire $|P_t|$. Write $W=P\setminus\varphi(|X|\setminus Q)$. On $W$, $\varphi$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] and locally quasi-finite. The explicit assertion in [lem-sfb-stack-separation-composition], that a proper locally quasi-finite algebraic space over a scheme is finite over it and a scheme, applies to $\varphi^{-1}W\to W$. Consequently this restriction is finite and its source is a scheme.

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), last paragraph, finite over an open containing the entire projective-space fibre

proof.text: Since $q$ is proper, $q(P\setminus W)$ is closed; it does not contain $t$ because $P_t\subseteq W$. Choose an affine open $V\ni t$ inside $T\setminus q(P\setminus W)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Then $P_V\subseteq W$. The preimage of this open under the finite scheme morphism $\varphi^{-1}W\to W$ is $X_V$, and the restriction $\varphi_V:X_V\to P_V$ is finite: on an affine open of $P_V$ it is the same finite ring map as before, using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. In particular $X_V$ is a scheme. Step 5 on the scheme test $X_V\to X$ identifies $\varphi_V$ with the morphism given by the restricted $s_i$ and identifies its hyperplane pullback with $L^{\otimes d}|_{X_V}$.

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), last paragraph, shrinking the base by closedness of projective space

proof.text: Compose with the isomorphism $\theta$ over $V$ of [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space], which on affine charts fixes every $T_i$ and hence matches $D_+(T_i)$ and the glued twists $\mathcal O(1)$ with their coordinate sections. By the quotient compatibility of step 5, $\theta\varphi_V$ pulls $\mathcal O(1)$ back to $L^{\otimes d}|_{X_V}$ with $T_i\mapsto s_i$, so it is the morphism $\varphi_{(L^{\otimes d},(s_i))}$ of [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] by the uniqueness stated there. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-morphism-chart-preimage], $(X_V)_{s_i}=\varphi_V^{-1}(D_+(T_i)_V)$. The target charts are affine because $V$ is affine, by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. Finiteness makes their inverse images affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. They cover $X_V$, and each $s_i$ is a section of the positive power $L^{\otimes d}$. Also $X_V$ is quasi-compact: its proper map to the affine, hence quasi-compact $V$ is quasi-compact, by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. These facts are exactly ampleness of $L_V$ in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; no extraction of a root of an ample power is needed. For every affine open $B\subseteq V$, $B\to V$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], so $X_B\to X_V$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. The affine pullback theorem [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-ample-invertible] gives ampleness of $L_B$. This is precisely the relative-ampleness conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0D3A (lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood), last paragraph, finite affine chart pullbacks prove ampleness directly
